summary: This figure compares three alternative node-number permutations for TopoOpt's double binary tree (DBT), the reduce communication pattern used to compute per-job traffic demand matrices. Each panel draws the same tree shape twice, stacked: a first binary tree whose non-root internal nodes get one half of the 16 node IDs and whose leaves get the other half, and a second binary tree that flips that assignment, so every node other than the two roots is an internal node in one tree and a leaf in the other, balancing each node's communication load. Panels (a), (b), and (c) keep this identical tree skeleton and simply reassign which of the 16 node IDs sits at each position, showing that many permutations can realize the same balanced double-binary-tree pattern, leaving room to also match it to the network topology.
summary_zh: 该图比较TopoOpt双二叉树(DBT)的三种节点编号排列：每组上下两棵树形状相同，节点在一棵树中为内部节点、在另一棵树中为叶子，实现通信负载均衡；(a)(b)(c)保持树形不变，仅改变16个编号的分配方式。
notes: Elements/relations enumerate panel (a) as the template (32 nodes, 30 edges: two 16-node trees where each node is internal in one tree and a leaf in the other); panels (b) and (c) share the identical tree shape with different number assignments. This matches the source-SVG histogram exactly (96 gray node fills = 32 x 3 panels, 90 blue strokes = 30 x 3 panels). worked_example is set to true because the specific node numbers are the entire content the reader checks. layout.panels mirrors the index's raw value (1) while layout.panel_count (3) reflects the three drawn alternatives, matching the convention used in sibling records.
